<reason>A wins through the stronger safety comparison and more direct answers under pressure. It explains why device limits cannot replace individualized screening and follow-up, while B repeatedly attacks one-time gatekeeping rather than the continuing care A proposes. B’s autonomy and blanket-restriction objections remain substantial, keeping this competitive. However, B overstates reversibility and never establishes that restriction-induced DIY harm outweighs expanded commercial exposure.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A exposes the faulty inference that safe prescribed home use makes screening redundant: screening, hardware limits, and follow-up can provide complementary protections. B concedes that screening can matter but does not adequately answer this distinction, continuing to contrast firmware with a mere permission slip.</best_rebuttal>
